lines: Clean feathers and straight shafts make trouble keep its distance.
A good bow hears trouble before the bell does.
A crooked feather makes a promise the arrow cannot keep.
Distance changes everything. Trouble looks smaller until it arrives.
The best warning is the one that reaches trouble before trouble reaches us.
Aim is not just the hand. It is patience deciding not to flinch.
Missed shots teach loudly, especially when everyone heard you brag first.
I once threw away a whole bundle because one shaft taught me suspicion.
There are nights when the bell rings and every arrow feels too few.
Mind the fletching table. Straight arrows do not happen by accident.
Give the fletching table room. Arrows works better without elbows in it.

Your face lands near the target, but the rest of the memory wobbles.
There was a hiss, a bite of gold, and then my thoughts found their fletching.
The memory is rough around the edges, but your face stayed in it.
I remember you. The arrow of it still shakes in the target.
I know you helped. I also remember why my hands still shake.
The cure left echoes behind. Stand where I can breathe around them.
Thunder shook the fletching table so hard bowstrings hummed at each crack, but everyone near me is still standing.
I checked bows, arrows, and string after the lightning, then counted heads. No one should be alone after a sky like that.
Near the fletching table, the bell sounded small under that thunder. We stayed inside and kept the doors watched.
That thunder made everyone quiet. I checked the bowstrings twice.
The sky can keep its lightning. I have bowstrings to set right.
I checked feathers, string, and dry sticks for sparks first, then checked faces for smoke and fear.
We passed water hand to hand and kept people away from the smoke. I checked the fletching table after.
Fresh arrows can wait. People come first.
We saved what we could reach around the fletching table, then stopped pretending things matter more than neighbors.
The smoke is thinning near the fletching table, but everyone is still sniffing the air like it might lie.
During a raid, fresh arrows can wait; who makes it behind a door matters more.
The horns stopped, but my hands near the fletching table still expect another wave from the road.
We counted living neighbors before bows, arrows, and string. That is the only count worth starting with.
Raiders came looking for easy emeralds. They found barred doors near the fletching table and a bell that would not stop ringing.
From the fletching table, I saw fear cross the square; then I saw courage get there first.
Night trouble tests the loose latch by the fletching table first. We are fixing those before sunset.
I stayed near the lane beyond bow range and listened for anyone calling from the dark.
Dawn gave the fletching table enough light to count wounds, missing blocks, and who made it home.
The dark tested everyone. Most of us passed by keeping a straight arrow between us and teeth.
We are safe enough near the fletching table, though every shadow is being inspected twice.
The wind threw sand through every crack. I am still cleaning grit out of the bowstring.
I checked bows, arrows, and string, then checked who was coughing too hard to answer.
Sand reached the fletching table, the hinges, and half our eyes, but no one has been reported missing.
A hard wind teaches a fletcher which doors actually close and which ones only pretend.
We are safe enough near the fletching table, though the whole village sounds like it is chewing gravel.
Fresh arrows can wait. Warm hands, clear paths, and full hearths come first.
Snow piled against the doors, but everyone near the fletching table found shelter.
Cold works quietly around the fletching table. We are checking on anyone who stayed quiet too long.
I am clearing ice off the arrowheads and watching for footprints that stop too soon.
We are alright for now near the fletching table. Keep the fires fed and the paths open.
Straight out, straight back. A good route flies true.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I will count that as good work.
That trip feathered wrong. I came home, but not without a bend in the shaft.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
You loosed that hurt at close range. I will remember the aim.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
The boat drifted, but it did not miss the mark entirely.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
That route you took me on flew about as straight as a warped arrow.
I remember following you through that road. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across that road taught me to ask more questions before walking.
That boat did not fly straight, but at least it floated straight enough.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
It kept its line under pressure. A steady hand is easier with proper tools.

Do not notch the same mistake twice.
I hear the words. Now keep your aim away from us.

Fine. Let this be the shot you meant to take.
Trust is easy to miss and hard to hit again. Try carefully.
Lost two arrows, kept my nerve. I will call that a fair trade.
My quiver is lighter, but so is my heart now that I am inside the village again.
I counted arrows until counting steps mattered more.
My hands remembered what to do before my head caught up.
I made it back with an empty quiver and a full respect for walls.
The road home felt like a target I could barely see.
A steady breath is harder when the dark is shouting.
I lost my aim for a moment. I did not lose the way home.
A bowstring complains before it betrays you. Most people do the opposite.
Straight arrows are made from crooked material and stubborn hands.
When the bell rings, I learn which arrows were practice and which were promises.
